title: Modbus: Enhanced reporting of invalid Modbus frames, exception field has been added
description:
Be more forgiving of traffic on TCP/UDP port 502 so that buggy implementations of Modbus/TCP can be more easily identified. Modbus/TCP is officially registered on TCP/UDP 502 so it _should_ be the primary protocol used there. Unfortunately, it doesn't have other strong heuristics besides the port number to easily identify buggy field values in an implementation.

Fixes #20599

added 1 commit

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20345/diffs?diff_id=1403338127&start_sha=099934979a8fa52dc8502ab5533453b9cbdbb825)
I understand the sentiment, but this is removing checks that are preventing packets that aren't Modbus to be classified as such. Perhaps the checks can be relaxed a little bit, but not removed.

But they are not removed. They are moved to dissect_mbtcp_pdu_common (line 436) and if an inconsistency is found, the error is reported through expert_add_info.
And still retained the requirement for a minimum length of 6 bytes (line 795).

Sample capture is included above. You can compare it in Wireshark with and without the modification.

The idea behind the original checks was to check _before_ making any dissection tree items if the protocol isn't Modbus.  We don't want the dissection to be "sorry this isn't Modbus, but that's all we can display".  Unfortunately, Modbus doesn't have the best heuristics for avoiding false positives.

You have provided an interesting sample capture and I'm trying to work with it without your patch applied.  You have definitely identified a bug/limitation, but your current fix is a bit aggressive towards Modbus (and the cost of potential incorrect dissection of other protocols).

What really stands out to me is the first packet.  Are there supposed to be 2 (or more) Modbus packets in there? "Manually" dissecting the bytes (Modbus is small enough that I can do that) it looks like the "extra/undissected" bytes aren't quite a real Modbus TCP header.
left review comments

Here is a little bit longer capture 

[Modbus2.pcapng](/uploads/87bc92e09870898846c93ed1d1dc71da/Modbus2.pcapng)

The cause of the error is a bug in the SW driver. Without my modification the erroneous data is silently unprocessed as Modbus.

Feel free to make any other change in the dissector to display the error.
Port 502 is standardized for Modbus, so no other services should run on this port and it should always be primarily treated as Modbus.

Unfortunately that's not reality.  While I think we can prefer IANA registered ports, other protocols intentionally use other/random ports for their data.  Modbus can also run on other (non 502) ports as well.  Unfortunately Modbus doesn't have strong enough heuristics on its own to be able to withstand things like an invalid protocol ID or an endian swapped length field.

I think I'll intentionally open up an issue about this (with the captures provided), and modify this MR with some potential ideas.

Thank you for improving my commit. You removed the modbus.exception field and you don't want it there?

It can then be difficult for a person to recognise what the exception arises from.
